candidates.tagline: Garmin made a $200 fitness tracker with no screen — your wrist knows nothing
candidates.story: Garmin launched the $200 CIRQA Smart Band on July 21, 2026 — a wrist-worn fitness tracker with zero display, meaning the device that is supposed to give you instant health data literally cannot show you your heart rate, steps, or calories without opening your phone; DC Rainmaker's hands-on review asked 'How on earth does a heart rate band not show me my actual current heart rate?' — and buyers are waiting up to eight weeks to find out.
candidates.why_funny: The whole point of a wrist device is the instant glance — Garmin built the exact opposite and sold out anyway.
candidates.alt: Garmin CIRQA Smart Band in black shown from the side against a white background — a minimal fabric band with a small rectangular sensor pod and a single physical button, no screen or display of any kind on the device

candidates.tagline: This $49 butt-face toy for ages 4+ just went viral in Australia for all the wrong reasons
candidates.story: Goliath Games launched Chester Cheeks worldwide on July 6, 2026 — a $49 interactive toy whose face is literally shaped like cartoon buttocks, which makes fart sounds and dances when children press, squeeze, or spread its cheeks; Australian Big W shoppers found it on July 30 and demanded a recall, with one parent calling it 'very inappropriate indeed' while Goliath markets it as 'perfect for parties and pranks.'
candidates.why_funny: The product team looked at a butt, thought 'children's face,' a global toy company approved it, and the only people who weren't in on the joke were the parents at the school-supply aisle.
candidates.alt: Chester Cheeks toy product packaging — a round smiling face that is unmistakably shaped from cartoon buttock forms, wearing oversized headphones, shown against colourful product art with the Butt Face logo
